_what: fork F5I: THE SELFTEST ROSTER, AS DATA. The gate's suite list used to exist three times -- as a hand-maintained tuple in tools/run_selftests.py, as a 43-arm strcmp chain in src/mh_dll/mh_nettest/net_selftest.cpp, and as a hand-written mode list in that chain's error message -- with nothing comparing them. This file is now the single list. run_selftests.py reads `suites` and `flaky` from here, and before running anything asserts that the exe's OWN `--list-suites` output equals the set recorded here for that exe; tools/check_selftest_roster.py asserts the same set against the table parsed out of the C++ source (the lint has no build, so it reads source where the driver reads the binary).
_order: `suites` is in the order run_selftests.py runs them, which is src/mh_dll/README.md's order and is load-bearing in at least one place: `hostintest`'s first arm is an open being REFUSED over an unanswered registry, so it must run before anything binds the regions. The C++ table is kept in the same order; the assertions compare SETS, because order is this file's business and a reordered table should not red the gate.
_exe: `exe` is WHICH EXECUTABLE answers to this suite, and since fork F5I S2 there are two. net_selftest.exe (src/mh_dll/mh_nettest) is the HOSTED arm -- no MH_LIBMH_BUILD, so every promotion seam and hook row compiles in and MH_CRT() names the original binary's VAs. libmh_selftest.exe (src/mh_dll/libmh_test, generated by tools/gen_libmh_vcxproj.py) is the STANDALONE arm (MH_LIBMH_BUILD + MH_SPINE_IN_IMAGE) compiling the same 628 roster TUs as the whole program. THE SPLIT IS BY SUBJECT, NOT BY SUITE (ruling R6): a suite whose subject is hosted-only machinery stays hosted even when its subject is spine code. That is why `statetest`, `bindtest` and `hostintest` are net-side -- statetest's subject is ST2, a region moving off its STOCK VA, and bindtest asserts the hosted answer to "where does each region live", and hostintest's first arm is an open REFUSED over an unanswered registry, while standalone every stock base is 0 by design (mh_regions.gen.h's MH_STOCK_BASE keeps original VAs out of libmh.lib's data), so all three would assert over a table of zeros and print green. The standalone side of that question is run_gate's libref unit, which stands the registry up and opens the inbound surface for real. 18 net_selftest / 15 libmh_selftest (logrottest joined the net side at mp:SES2). tools/run_selftests.py builds both and runs each row on the exe named here; tools/check_selftest_roster.py asserts, per exe, that the gate-flagged set of that exe's SUITE_TABLE is exactly the set of rows naming it -- so a suite cannot end up gated in both or in neither.
_checks: `checks` is the total of the `N checks, M failures` line(s) a suite prints on a green plain run, recorded 2026-09-16 from the exe built at fork HEAD cf777b51 by tools/prove_suite_identity.py --record. It is SUM, not last: `crttest` is two halves in one invocation (sprintf family + the five other vendored headers) and prints a line for each. null means the suite prints no such line at all -- the seven transport/orchestrator suites report by exit code and prose -- so for those the identity of a run is its exit code plus its normalised transcript and nothing here. The number is a FLOOR that grows with the domain, not a contract: it is here so that a suite which silently stops registering half its assertions is visible, since such a suite still exits 0.
_seamtest: `seamtest` is deliberately ABSENT. It is a KNOWN pre-existing failure that crashes on the baseline commit too (verified 2026-07-25 by stashing). Adding it would make the gate permanently red and train everyone to ignore the script. It is a suite, so it is in the C++ table -- but without the `gate` flag, which is why the flag exists.
_why_field: `why` is the comment run_selftests.py carried above that row, moved here verbatim-in-substance when the tuple was deleted. It is the record of WHY a suite is in the gate -- usually the defect that got it added -- and null only for the rows that predate the practice of explaining one.
_exes: WHERE EACH EXE IS BUILT FROM, added at fork F5I S4 so that a tool routing a suite does not have to carry its own copy of the two project paths. `vcxproj` is the MSBuild project that produces that exe, `dir` is its source directory, and `staged` is the basename the build bat stages into the %TEMP% staging directories. Every value in the `exe` column above must be a key here -- tools/coverage.py and tools/mutate.py assert exactly that before they build anything, so a third exe added to the roster reds them instead of silently building the wrong project.
_flaky: The suites that operate big graphs of heap buffers, i.e. whose failure mode includes DYING. run_selftests.py repeats these on the PLAIN pass, where a crash is the only symptom corruption produces. `simtest` joined them at SIM0 (2026-08-08): its fixture is ~4 MB of real-extent rosters and the sim writes them, so it is in exactly the population that produced both historical 0xC0000374s.

suites.why: mp:U40 (2026-09-17). A client whose link died could never make another one in the same process: g_started latched true for the life of the process (MH_Net_Shutdown had been deleted at F4B for having no callers), so MH_Net_InitEx early-returned and the discovery poll's connect kick -- gated on !MH_Net_IsStarted() -- never fired again. Measured in the 2026-09-01 internet session: `handshake OK` appears EXACTLY ONCE in a 16-minute client log while the host re-advertised its new lobby to peers=0. This suite stages the link death with linktest's mute-peer trick and then asserts the two halves the rig cannot: a re-dial makes a genuinely NEW connection (a SECOND host-assigned WELCOME, counted by the host as a second accept), and a re-dial that FAILS leaves the transport stopped and retryable rather than wedged -- which is the S8 retry path the seam depends on.

ADDED 2026-09-08 (CRT-X87 step 2). mh/fp/x87.h's two helpers were inline x87 and are now C++; this keeps a verbatim copy of the assembly as the reference arm and re-proves the equality at BOTH precision settings every run. Falsified by hand once: removing the _PC_64 install reds it.
ADDED 2026-09-02 (LT0). The lib_trans domain oracle's expectation layer: the RNG-family golden vectors + batch-A wrapper contracts, pinned against the verified rng_next body.

ADDED 2026-09-02 (D24). Which inbound frame a FULL transport queue may destroy. The defect it guards is silent and luck-dependent -- a peer whose main thread froze lost 15 replicated orders to the old drop-oldest policy -- so a green rig campaign cannot stand in for it.

ADDED 2026-09-17 (SES0). The UUIDv7 match_id, the v3 SESSION_INFO/JOIN records and the host's ADMIT decision. It carries the two acceptance clauses the rig physically cannot reach: a pre-SES0 client's JOIN being refused BY VERSION with a named reason, and a pre-SES0 DECODER refusing a v3 advert instead of best-effort parsing it -- there is no old client to run, so both refusals exist only offline. ADDED 2026-09-17 (SES1). The per-SESSION run directory: the directory NAME, the rollover state machine, and the session.json / SESSION_BEGIN / SESSION_END record. Three of SES1's five acceptance clauses are claims about a name and a transition table -- three matches without a restart yielding three DISTINCT directories while the host's ~1 Hz re-advert of the same id yields none, a run that never joins a lobby landing in a `menu` directory, and session.json carrying the match_id in a form a tool reads without parsing prose (including at OPEN, which is the only record a crashed peer leaves). It also pins the GLOB CONTRACT -- a directory name still ends in `_<role>` -- because the rename touched every folder in the tree and mp_run.py/test_ui.py find peers by `*_host`/`*_client`/`*_solo`: had that stopped holding, the rig would have reported peers as never started rather than going red. The remaining two clauses (the directories really appear, every stream lands in them) stay rig work; they are claims about CreateDirectory and about a dozen writers.

ADDED 2026-09-17 (mp:SES2). The log-stream SIZE CAP and its one-generation rotation. ADDED 2026-09-17 (mp:T0). The UDP packet format (plan D2): the 18-byte authenticated header, the 64-entry replay window, the three channels and the connect token. Its centre is a directory of FIXTURE FILES under src/mh_net_proto/test/fixtures/udp/ that this suite AND `cargo test -p relay` both read -- an encoder agreeing with its own decoder is one implementation agreeing with itself, so the claim worth gating is that two independent decoders accept and refuse the same committed bytes. The four acceptance cases (round-trip, a tampered byte failing the MAC, a replayed sequence dropped, a 1201-byte datagram refused) are each a committed fixture rather than only an in-process assertion. Milliseconds; no socket, no rig. The suite's `--fuzz <seconds>` arm is NOT part of the gate -- it is a timed run under the ASan build, reported per item, because a gate row that costs ten minutes is a gate nobody runs.

ADDED 2026-09-17 (mp:T1). The UDP transport's own oracle, and the only place two of its acceptance clauses can be STATED: ordered gap-free delivery under a loss rate 127.0.0.1 cannot produce, and the attribution of what repaired each loss. It prints a per-arm counter line rather than a check total, because the number that matters is `gap stalls 0` beside a non-zero synthetic-loss count, not how many assertions ran.

ADDED 2026-09-18 (mp:T3). The link-measurement ARITHMETIC, with no link. Everything T3 adds is measured on a path, and a path is the one thing this machine cannot stage: each of T3's three rig clauses needs two VMs, net_shim.py in front of them and several minutes, and a red run cannot say whether the estimator, the sampler or the controller was wrong. So the arithmetic lives in an I/O-free header (src/mh_dll/mh_net_udp/udp_stats.h) and this suite pins it: RFC 6298 §2 rules 2.2 and 2.3 against hand-computed vectors (the rule-2.3 pair is also the MUTATION CHECK on the assignment order -- RTTVAR must use the OLD SRTT, so 47.5 passes and the swapped-order 46.25 does not); a synthetic 80 +/- 20 stream standing in for the shim, asserting the same 'SRTT within 10% of 80, RTTVAR non-zero' the rig clause asks for; a steady-link negative control where RTTVAR and IPDV must collapse; a 60/100 alternation that separates IPDV (a pair statistic, -> 40) from RTTVAR (deviation from the mean, -> 20); the probe table refusing an echo it never sent; the 256-packet loss window (complete -> 0 pm, 1-in-20 -> ~50 pm, an in-window REORDER -> 0, too few packets -> -1 rather than a confident 0); the lateness percentiles, including that tail95 is the LOW end under L0's positive-is-margin sign; and the adaptive controller's decision function driven through all four verdicts -- the 200 ms clause (grows on the FIRST decision, capped at a doubling), the hysteresis band, the three clean windows before the first 4% step, and a clean link settling EXACTLY on the configured minimum and staying there over 500 windows. Milliseconds; no socket, no rig.

ADDED 2026-09-17 (mp:T1b). U40's restart rule, asked of the OTHER transport module. U40 fixed mh_net.dll only; mh_net_udp.dll's InitEx still early-returned on a started transport, so a client that finished a match over `[net] transport=udp` could not dial the re-created lobby -- the same dead end, one module over. It cannot be an arm of `relinktest`: that suite drives the MH_Net_* exports, which in net_selftest.exe are the TCP module's (udp_transport.cpp defines the same 23 symbols and two definitions do not link), so the UDP side is reached through mh::netudp::Endpoint the way udploopbacktest reaches it -- which is also why the restart lives IN the endpoint and the module's InitEx is a thin g_started bookkeeper over it. Two endpoints on 127.0.0.1: the host's watchdog retires a mute client, the client re-dials on an already-started transport, and the host counts a SECOND completed handshake (hs_done, not a WELCOME -- host_assign is off here, because a WELCOME rides the reliable stream and a peer that has received stream bytes acks forever, which would keep the victim alive). Then the traffic arm (a handshake that delivers no byte would pass every count) and the negative arm: UDP has no connect(), so a dial into the dark cannot fail at start -- what must hold is that it leaves the transport dialable, proven by a THIRD dial that lands. ~13 s. MUTATION-CHECKED: restoring the pre-T1b `if (m_started) return true;` turns 8 of the 19 checks red.

ADDED 2026-09-19 (mp:R7a). The MH_NetConfig relay fields, offline. R7a gave a peer with `[net] relay` set a direct mode again by moving the relay-vs-direct decision out of mh_net_udp.dll (which read the ini and tunnelled EVERY connection) into mh.dll, and making it travel in an APPENDED MH_NetConfig.relay_addr (empty = a direct dial) + relay_room. Three properties are testable with no rig and each is the failure a silent regression would be: (1) the config field's DEFAULT is no relay -- a zero-initialised MH_NetConfig (what every self-test, the force-entry path and a forgetful caller get) carries an empty relay_addr, so the direct mode R7a restored is the default rather than something every caller must opt into; (2) the two fields are APPENDED -- relay_addr after rx_timeout_ms and relay_room the last member, so the TCP module and any pre-R7a reader address every field above them at unchanged offsets and ignore the trailing bytes (checked by offsetof); (3) the TCP module (net_transport.cpp, this exe's MH_Net_*) is INDIFFERENT to them -- a TCP host init carrying a relay address still starts as the plain direct host it is, proving it never reads the field a transport with no relay cannot act on.

ADDED 2026-09-18 (mp:T2). CHANNEL C, the bulk reliable chunk transfer: the third layer, above T0's packet format and T1's channel-A byte stream. Two arms need no sockets. Arm 0 is the LANE VOCABULARY -- an MSG_ORDER frame and a completed chunk are both in lanes no eviction path can reach, a bare 9-byte horizon is the one that is, and a 10-byte one is protected; a vocabulary where nothing was evictable would pass every other check in the file. Arm 0b is the PIECE BOUND: T0's `piece_decode` ties `total` to `chunk_len` but nothing ties `piece_len` to the INDEX, so a peer declaring the last piece of a 16384-byte chunk as a full 1100 walks 116 bytes off the assembly buffer -- the arm shows the ENCODER accepts that frame and the RECEIVER refuses it, then feeds the well-formed run of the same chunk through to show the check is a bound and not a wall. The other six run on two in-process endpoints over 127.0.0.1, for udploopbacktest's reason -- a child process talks to a real loopback socket and 127.0.0.1 drops nothing, so `1 MiB crosses at 5% loss` would have no way to produce the 5%. (1) a clean mebibyte, byte-identical, and NO retransmit at all -- a clean link that used the repair path means the window arithmetic is wrong rather than that the link was lucky; (2) the same mebibyte at 5% injected loss in BOTH directions, asserting the injection fired (74 datagrams destroyed, 56 pieces repeated) before it believes the hash; (3) the receiver KILLED mid-transfer with Endpoint::stop() and dialled again, asserting the chunk frontier is the same NUMBER after the restart as before it -- so the sender resumes at the last acknowledged chunk, and exactly N chunks are delivered, none twice; (4) the receiver comes back having forgotten everything (a restarted PROCESS, placement-new'd), so its frontier is zero while the sender is mid-transfer and the sender must REWIND to it -- this arm exists because mutation-testing arm 3 produced a real DEADLOCK in a sender that could only advance; (5) the application STOPS draining, so the never-evictable lane fills, REFUSES, and the transfer applies backpressure -- `lane_refused > 0` AND `lane_evicted == 0`, which is D24's question asked of the one queue whose contents are by definition not supersedable; (6) the `[net] bulk_selftest_mb` synthetic path, so the rig knob is not code whose first run is on the rig; and (7) PACING -- channel-A delivery latency idle versus with a mebibyte crossing underneath, which is the offline half of the item's rig clause and a different claim with a different instrument, not a substitute (the rig measures the game's frame pacing; this measures the transport's own latency while channel C is saturated). It is precise because both peers share one clock: the sender stamps GetTickCount() into the record and the receiver subtracts. Measured 2026-09-18: p95 16 ms idle and 16 ms with the transfer, max 32 both; the budget asserted is one endpoint tick, which is exactly what BULK_BURST spends. It prints per-arm counter lines as well as a check total, like udploopbacktest. ~40 s. MUTATION-CHECKED twice, both measured before arms 0, 0b and 4 were added (so against a 40-check run): deleting the retransmit arm of Channel::tick reds 6 (the lossy and resume arms; the CLEAN arm stays green, which is the point of asserting zero retransmits there), and clearing the bulk channel in Endpoint::stop() -- the obvious tidy-up, since stop() memsets everything else -- reds 4, all in the resume arm and named exactly by `the chunk frontier SURVIVED the stop (10 before, 0 after)`. That second mutation is also what FOUND arm 4: the mutant did not merely lose the prefix, it DEADLOCKED, because the sender could only advance.

ADDED 2026-09-18 (mp:R3). THE HOLE-PUNCH PROMOTION STATE MACHINE, with no network. Every one of R3's four acceptance clauses is a rig clause -- two VMs, a Windows firewall rule applied over ssh, a relay process, minutes per answer -- and a red rig run says only that a pair stayed relayed: not whether the candidate codec, the probe cadence, the promotion rule or the demotion timer was at fault. So the decision half was written as a pure function of (state, event, time) in src/mh_dll/mh_net_udp/udp_punch.cpp, holding no socket and reading no clock, and this suite drives it as a table of milliseconds. EIGHT ARMS, and one of them exists because a rig run found a real bug that a green rig run had already hidden. A is the candidate codec against the same refusals the Rust half asserts over the same bytes (leg.rs's tests): every truncation refused rather than read as a shorter list, a trailing byte, a count over MAX_CANDS, an unknown address family, an output buffer too small. B/C is the happy path -- two candidates in, both probed at once, echoes back, the peer's own probe seen, PROMOTED, with the elapsed punch readable off the struct -- followed by the RULE stated as two NEGATIVES, which is the mutation check on it: acked-but-never-heard must stay relayed for thirty seconds, and so must heard-but-never-acked; an || where the code has && passes every other arm in the file and fails exactly these two. It also pins the nonce discipline (an echo consumed twice credits nothing, a nonce nobody sent credits nothing, zero is never valid). D is the two probe cadences and the ten-second window between them -- the only part of 'direct within 10 s of match start' this side controls. E is the arm that makes punching work against a NAT whose mapping toward the peer is not the one the relay observed: a probe from an address NOBODY advertised becomes a candidate, is probed, and the pair promotes onto it and not onto the advertised one; plus the table ceiling refusing the overflow by name. F/G is demotion on silence -- nineteen seconds of ANSWERED keepalives keep the path, the timer then fires exactly at DEAD_MS and not a millisecond earlier, a promoted pair keeps ONE path warm rather than every loser it collected, and the search restarts afterwards including on the path that just died because the commonest cause is a rebinding. F2 IS THE ARM WORTH READING: a path whose INBOUND half is busy and whose outbound half is dead must still demote. The first implementation counted any authenticated datagram from the peer as liveness, which is evidence of peer->us and says nothing about us->peer; on the rig (2026-09-18) a mid-match firewall cut demoted the client in 3.0 s, never demoted the host, and the run stalled at step 555 -- and an EARLIER rig run of the same configuration had gone green because the host reached its step budget before the consequences arrived. Restoring that one line reds F2 and nothing else in the file. H is [net] force_relay=1: it takes no candidates, sends no probe, never promotes over sixty seconds of a fully validated path, and pins a pair that is ALREADY direct back to the relay at once. I is the GetTickCount WRAP: 49.7 days after boot the counter goes 0xFFFFFFFF -> 0, and a comparison of two stamps is wrong across it while an unsigned subtraction is right -- the arm drives twenty seconds of traffic straight across zero and asserts no spurious demotion, then that the timer still FIRES across it. Milliseconds; no socket, no rig.

ADDED 2026-09-19 (mp:R6). The HOST'S relay room minter (udp_room.h): a host's room used to be its `[net] port`, so on the shared VPS relay the second player to host was refused `room_busy` until the first lobby ended (measured: 30 refusals over 16 s while a killed run's slot aged out). Now a random 30-bit code is minted per tunnel start and re-minted, at most BUSY_RETRIES times, on `room_busy`. The rig cannot stage two hosts on one relay (one box, one exclusive UDP port per lane), so the two-hosts clause, the retry bound (its mutation check: a `>` for the `>=` passes every other arm), the redraw of 0 / the avoided room, the crash-relaunch clause (a fresh minter never returns a stale room it was told to avoid) and the RNG-failure refusal are all proved here over an injected RNG.

ADDED 2026-09-19 (mp:R3e). THE HOST TUNNEL'S PER-PEER SLOTS, RELEASED. udp_relay.cpp holds three tables keyed by the relay handle -- one loopback socket per remote peer (so the endpoint sees distinct clients), one punch, one pair-key set -- MAX_REMOTE (8) of each, and until R3e a slot once used was held until the tunnel stopped: the ninth distinct peer to join a lobby over its life got no socket and no punch, and its join silently never completed. The tunnel has no signal of its own that a peer left (the relay tells a host nothing when a client drops, and its one `no_peer` refusal names no handle), so R3e made the ENDPOINT the owner -- a slot lives while Endpoint::knows_addr holds a conn or a live handshake for its loopback address, asked once a second past a 5 s grace -- and this suite drives the REAL tunnel against a STAND-IN relay and a stand-in endpoint on loopback, with the ownership predicate being the suite's own table. Nine sequential harness joins would be nine lobby walks on a lane pool with no headroom (TL-LANEPOOL). THREE ARMS, ~13 s: A joins eight fake handles (each a DATA then a CAND from the stand-in relay) and asserts eight DISTINCT loopback source ports at the endpoint and a PROBE naming each handle at the candidate the relay offered; a ninth while all eight are held gets neither and the refusal is logged -- the cap is real, and this is what every ninth join looked like before the fix (measured with the sweep disabled: 10 of the 20 checks red, every one in B and C -- 'the ninth join gets a loopback socket', 'gets a punch', the release count at 0 -- and the tunnel logging `no loopback socket left` for every handle from 9 up). B takes the eight out of the predicate, waits for exactly eight release lines and none inside the first second (a release inside the grace would be a slot freed before the endpoint could have registered its handshake), then joins 9 and 10 and asserts a socket and a punch each. C is the orphan rule: a CAND from a handle that never sends DATA -- a PSK holder probing under made-up handles -- holds a punch slot (it is probed) and is released by the sweep while 9 and 10, still held, are not; six more then join to a full table of eight and the next is refused as in A. Nothing promotes and no pair key is minted here (the probe target never answers, the endpoint never replies); that is udppunchtest's and the rig's.

ADDED 2026-09-18 (mp:X1). THE CHUNKED SNAPSHOT PIPELINE, the first consumer of T2's channel C and the one plan D7 names three uses for (join-in-progress, desync recovery, MP save/load). udpbulktest proves a megabyte of synthetic bytes crosses; this proves a WORLD crosses -- a real mh::state::world::capture() blob, 829 bound regions and ~8.2 MB, the RNG channels among them (mp:R-rng-snapshot) -- and that importing what the receiver assembled reproduces the CAPTURING peer's content hash and lockstep pair. One process, one arena, because libmh_bind_regions is process-global: fill, capture and record the hashes (this is the host at step N), move the blob over two real endpoints with a real loss dial, then POISON the arena with 0xCD -- which agrees with nothing -- and import. The poison is the peer boundary; after it the only route to the capturing peer's numbers is bytes that crossed a socket. SIX ARMS. F (no sockets, milliseconds) round-trips the manifest and then asks for a DIFFERENT refusal code from each of seven negatives: a flipped magic (ERR_MAGIC), a bumped format (ERR_FORMAT), a body_len moved by 4 MiB so the chunk count disagrees (ERR_SHAPE), a tampered chunk-hash entry and a tampered root (both ERR_ROOT), a corrupted body chunk (ERR_CHUNK_HASH, and the verified prefix stops at it so resume_chunk names it), a missing chunk (the gate stays shut, body() hands out nothing, ERR_INCOMPLETE), and a destination too small (refused AT THE MANIFEST, before a body byte exists). C moves the real capture at 0% loss and asserts a clean link needed NO retransmit. L is the headline clause -- the same capture at 5% injected loss in both directions, asserting the injection fired before it believes the hash -- and both C and L end in the same comparison: content hash, lockstep combined and state, and the three RNG channel regions byte-for-byte. R is the arm the manifest exists for: the sender's own composer spoils one chunk, so the piece SHA-256 on the wire is the SHA of the corrupt bytes and the TRANSPORT sees nothing wrong (rx_sha_fail 0) -- only the hash vector committed to before the transfer can refuse it, and that refusal rewinds the receiver's frontier, which is the whole re-request protocol (there is no NAK frame). T kills the link mid-transfer, keeps the verified prefix, brings a new link up and restores the frontier to resume_chunk(); the assertion is not that the transfer finishes but that every body chunk was verified EXACTLY ONCE across the restart, which a restart-from-zero would fail. N is all-or-nothing at the second layer: world::import() handed a blob one chunk short refuses AND leaves the poisoned arena byte-for-byte untouched, compared against a witness copy rather than against a hash.

ADDED 2026-09-18 (mp:X2). THE MAP DOWNLOAD, with no game and -- for six of its seven arms -- no socket. X2's four acceptance clauses are all rig clauses, and a red rig run says only 'the two peers did not agree about a map': not whether the hash was taken over the wrong bytes, the stored name was built wrong, the resolver preferred a name over a content, the Start gate's predicate was inverted, or a delivered blob was written without being re-checked. SEVEN ARMS. A is the STORED NAME, the one string the writer, the resolver and a human reading a directory listing all have to agree on: '<stem>.<16 hex>.<ext>', the hash inserted before the LAST dot so the extension survives (the extension is what picks the loose map directory over the campaign one), an extension-less base, and a buffer too small REFUSING rather than falling back to the base name -- that fallback would be the one file this scheme exists to never write. It also pins the recogniser's negatives, including the character-class trap the first implementation had: comparing against a rebuilt sample string made a base's own 'f' a hex wildcard. B is the WIRE: SESSION_INFO v5 and JOIN v5 round-tripping, a v4 advert still decoding with its own last field intact and the map hash read as NO CLAIM rather than as a hash of zero, a v6 advert refused outright, the JOIN carrying the JOINER's hash and never an echo of the advert (an echo would make every mismatch look like agreement), and a v4 JOIN refused as an old protocol BY NAME -- because a peer that never says which map it holds makes the Start gate vacuously true for itself. C is the FILE LAYER over a real scratch directory with real files (a mock would only assert that the mock agrees with itself), stepping one thing on disk at a time: absent, then the joiner's OWN same-named file of DIFFERENT content and the SAME LENGTH -- which must NOT match, the item's whole point, and the equal length is what stops a size compare passing for a hash -- then the host's content stored and resolving to the stored path -- under the content-addressed NAME and in the DOWNLOAD DIRECTORY, which is outside the map directory entirely, with NOTHING written beside the base name. Both halves are asserted because both were wrong once: a copy beside the player's maps would list in the picker (and the local rig's lanes share one Maps by symlink), and a subdirectory of Maps is worse -- llm_mp_mappicker_populate_list scans Maps for SUB-FOLDERS before it scans for *.mpm, so a download folder became the picker's pre-selected first row and a rig host never reached its lobby. The arm also compares the joiner's own file byte-for-byte against a witness still in memory. D is the refusal AT THE WRITE: the transfer proves the bytes CROSSED intact, which is a different claim from 'these are the bytes the advert named', so store() re-hashes; no correct host will ever send the wrong file, so this is the only place that second check can be driven at all. The arm also shows a refused store left NO file behind for the resolver to find on a later run. E is the OPEN REDIRECT, which is what lets the load resolve by hash WITHOUT renaming the map in game memory: current_map_data reaches Planet[31] and `planets` is a hashed determinism region, so a peer that renamed its map would red the determinism gate with a 'desync' that is really a filename. The base name is served the stored file case-insensitively and keeps its directory prefix, and every other path the game opens passes through untouched -- which matters because this sits on the game's single file-open wrapper, forty call sites, everything from Msgs.dat to a screenshot. F is the START GATE as a predicate over what seated peers REPORTED, with both halves asserted against each other, because a gate that is always shut and a gate that is always open each pass one of them: open with nobody seated, shut and NAMING the peer when one reports a different hash, unchanged when a second peer that already holds it joins, open once the first peer's re-JOIN reports our hash -- which is also 'a joiner already holding the content transfers nothing', asserted as host_next_peer_needing_map() == -1 rather than as a rig counter that stayed at zero -- open again after a departed peer leaves, and open for everyone when the host makes no claim at all, since a stock map is install-identical by construction. W is the WIRE END TO END: a 180 KB map across two real UDP endpoints through mp:X1's snapshot pipeline, stored under its content name, resolved, redirected, the stored file compared byte-for-byte to the host's map and the joiner's own file to its witness. Port argument plus 400, the next free slot after udpbulktest's +200 and udpsnaptest's +300.
